reviewer.name: Claude Sonnet, fresh subagent (cold reader 2)
reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-26 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session)

evidence: Read Appendix G whole first. The draft ('Borrow some from someone else if you need to, but make sure they're stable and not someone who will try to direct your trip.') sits in CONTEXT.txt once, exactly, as the last sentence of the opening paragraph, right after 'I’d learn the inner child work sober first, with enough Nurturer and Protector in the room before you go deep (see the inner child reparenting section).' and before the next paragraph's 'Do not do it to try to FORCE yourself ...'. It does what the_change says: one Emulate sentence in place of the one sentence from his inner child guide. Meaning against SOURCE ('Borrowed is fine, as long as it’s from someone steady who won’t try to run your trip for you.', where 'Borrowed' is the Nurturer and Protector of the sentence before, borrowed from someone else): same three points in the same order (borrowing is fine; from someone stable; who must not take over the trip). 'Borrowed' becomes 'some', which echoes 'enough Nurturer and Protector' one sentence earlier; 'steady' becomes 'stable'; 'won’t try to run your trip for you' becomes 'not someone who will try to direct your trip' ('direct' is a notch more formal than 'run ... for you' but names the same worry, a lender who takes charge). Two small shifts, neither a new claim: the blanket 'is fine' becomes 'if you need to', which fits 'enough' in the sentence before, and 'as long as' becomes 'make sure'. The one point where I slowed is 'some': in an appendix about substances, 'Borrow some' could for a beat be taken as borrowing substances. I do not think a careful reader keeps that reading, because the sentence before says 'sober first' and 'enough Nurturer and Protector in the room' (enough, then some), and the rest of this sentence ('stable', 'not someone who will try to direct your trip') only fits a person who sits with you. The source's 'Borrowed' needed the same look back, so the draft is no less clear than the words it replaces, and arguably clearer (C02 not tripped; 'they' lands on 'someone else' through 'not someone who'). Seam and voice: it reads as the same friendly, direct advice as the neighbouring 'I’d learn the inner child work sober first' and the appendix's imperatives; 'make sure' and the loose 'stable and not someone who' are speech-like, and I heard no second writer, no tidy summary and no hedge he would not write ('if you need to' is of a kind with the appendix's own '(If you can't give it to the child, try to deal with why you can't ...)'). The paragraph ends on a practical safeguard, a new consideration and not a moral or restatement (T20, T28, T29 not tripped). Rows: I found no row actually happening. T10: 'if you need to' is the stock permission tag, but here it is local (need = not enough Nurturer and Protector, from the sentence before) and it sits with a real safeguard, so I did not count it. T22: it instructs, but with a reason and a stance. T12 and T16: 'stable and not someone who ...' is one positive/negative pairing carried over from 'steady who won’t try' in the source, with no reveal. T21: one sentence with a permission and two conditions, as in the source. T15: the sentence is rebuilt, not only re-worded, and no other tell stays. T26: 'someone' twice in one sentence is a parallel that does a job. T01 to T09, T11, T13, T14, T17 to T19, T23 to T25, T27, C01, C03 and C04 are absent (no first person, no scene, no filler, no colon, no tic word, the inner child is not named). Small notes, not defects: the writer's ledger lines for T14 and T15 say the sentence 'puts back' the author's point or words, which this change does not do (it is Emulate's sentence as it is), so I judged those rows on the words and both are absent; and 'they're' has a straight apostrophe beside the curly one in 'I’d', but the appendix already mixes both (older text has 'If you've', 'you're'), so it is no seam. Linter findings: 'D9 follows the source order' is accepted, because one sentence replaces one sentence and there is no sequence to reorder; a permission followed by its conditions is the natural order, and it notices something (the lender must not take over the trip), so T13 and T09 are absent. 'E36/E41 heavy second person' is accepted, because it is two second-person words ('you need', 'your trip') in 24 words, a short-sentence ratio (8.3), lower than the source's two in 19; the paragraph is addressed to 'you' throughout, and this is a safety caution with a reason, not coaching or reassurance.
